title: Visiting Student - XSD - Koda, Ryota - 10.21.26
description: This project proposes a real-time workflow for 3D X-ray ptychography that uses a sample-specific surrogate model to reduce reconstruction time. In 3D ptychography, a sample is illuminated from many angles, and a 2D image is recovered for each angle with iterative phase retrieval (e.g., ePIE) before the images are combined into a 3D volume. Because the phase retrieval is repeated for every direction, it dominates the total runtime. Earlier surrogate-model studies sped up this step but did not evaluate the whole workflow, and they typically required a training dataset prepared in advance. The proposed method instead builds the surrogate model on-the-fly. First, directional subsampling selects a subset of the projection angles. ePIE is run only on those angles, and the resulting diffraction pattern and object image pairs form a small training set. A surrogate model is trained on this set and predicts initial object estimates for the remaining angles. After preprocessing, these predictions initialize a second ePIE pass. The workflow will run on GPUs. Additional work will include the development of a foundation surrogate model for diverse samples and testing other surrogate architectures. title: Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer – EDA Clusters
description: Securing NVIDIA 's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack. The workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for an off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. You'll be an individual contributor on Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters, the team that implements security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA 's hardware engineers design silicon on - spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud. You will sit alongside the engineers who run these clusters 24x7, close enough to deploy a control, investigate a behavior, and change the running environment yourself. This is hands-on build work, not control review. You'll decide where conventional tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and then engineer the alternative. If your depth is in large-scale compute, networking, or storage infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job, and you've carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you're who we want to talk to. We don't expect fluency in every security product category. We expect you to own outcomes and pick up the remaining domain breadth fast. Security engineering here is engineering: code, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure - not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets. What You'll Be Doing: Build and operate security controls and telemetry for EDA compute, storage, and networking - design, ship to production, then own them. Engineer around hard constraints. Protect multi-day, high-value compute jobs without degrading them. Where heavyweight in-node agents are not viable, build the workable answer instead. Make the network and platform the control plane. Protection can't depend solely on what runs inside the node. Instrument for detection. Collect and normalize security signals from the fleet into our SIEM, and build the detections and dashboards that turn it into something actionable. Log collection alone is not monitoring. Investigate and respond. Chase down EDA-specific threats and exposure, and execute containment and remediation hands-on with infrastructure and service owners. Automate enforcement and evidence. Infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state, with compliance evidence produced as an engineering output rather than a manual exercise. Run the lifecycle of the security technologies you own: selection, rollout, operation, and eventual replacement. Work across boundaries. Partner directly with data center operations, IT storage and networking, network engineering, CSP teams, and NVIDIA 's central security organization on shared outcomes. Think like an adversary. Threat modeling and mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute. What We Need To See: 8+ years of hands-on infrastructure or infrastructure-security engineering across on-prem and cloud enviro

description: About the Role What if AI could research antitrust law as precisely as a competition lawyer? Right now, it can't. Concurrences .com : The canonical antitrust platform since 2004. 100k+ articles, 20 years of case law, 120+ countries, ~50,000 professionals. Editorial board includes William Kovacic (former FTC Chair) and Mario Monti (former EU Commissioner). Now building Concurrences .AI — powering Claude, ChatGPT, and enterprise copilots to research competition law correctly. What You'll Do Evaluate AI outputs for legal accuracy: does it cite the right case? Does it confuse EU merger control with Brazilian CADE enforcement? Build evaluation frameworks that define what "correct" means across antitrust domains — cartels, mergers, abuse of dominance, state aid Design instructions that help the AI reason through legal problems with the precision of an antitrust specialist Test the system from a legal perspective — find the edge cases, the jurisdiction mismatches, the reversed precedents Write evaluation scripts using AI coding tools (no engineering background needed) What You Have Law degree (completed or final year) with strong academic foundations. Antitrust coursework or experience is a plus — but if you have solid legal training and are keen to learn competition law deeply, we want to hear from you You've tried Claude, ChatGPT, or another LLM and noticed it doesn't always get things right Strong English writing. French is a plus but not required Curiosity about AI + law — you want to explore how AI can serve legal research, not just practice law the way it's always been done Compensation €1,200/month, paid in EUR via Wise. Independent contractor, monthly invoicing. Fully remote. Async-first with regular mentoring sessions. Learn competition law and AI evaluation on the job — we invest in your growth. Start: ASAP. We believe the future of finance operations is not faster clicking: it’s no clicking at all 🫳 🎤 Finance teams shouldn’t spend their days moving data from one screen to another. Software should do the operational work, and humans should focus on reviewing, approving, and making the decisions that matter. title: TUM Project Study: Earned LinkedIn Media for Enterprise
description: About us Mediacharge GmbH is a Munich-based, internationally oriented marketing agency with ten years of experience in cutting-edge marketing for international enterprises. Operating in 14 languages, we combine first-tier strategic consulting with hands-on operational excellence, measured against business results. Project description (TUM Project) This project study explores what turns an enterprise’s own people into LinkedIn voices that measurably drive Sales, Recruiting or Employer Brand. Using Mediacharge and its enterprise clients as the case environment, it examines how earned media, meaning content published by real people rather than paid brand channels, creates business impact. The project combines a business strategy perspective - objectives, the right people and measurable outcomes - with a content and platform perspective, focusing on talent profiles, content types, success patterns and the time it takes to build an effective voice. Objectives of the project study to classify enterprise objectives for earned LinkedIn media (Sales, Recruiting, Employer Brand), to identify which talent profiles and content types work best for each objective, to derive success patterns, including what it takes and how long it takes to see results, to develop one strategy blueprint per objective and an impact model to measure business effect. Main task and methodology Students explore the topic through research, interviews and real enterprise cases (month 1), classify goals, talent profiles and success patterns (month 2), and build strategy blueprints, a final report and a pitch to Mediacharge leadership (month 3). Recommended methods include desk research, expert interviews, enterprise case analysis, benchmarking and impact modelling. Student requirements Students are fascinated by marketing at international enterprise scale, work analytically and build things that hold up in practice. Strong results open the door to a next conversation with Mediacharge. Project scope and application Preferred scope: 3 months in three phases: Explore, Analyse, Build Number of students: 3–5 Supervision: A Mediacharge supervisor with direct input from enterprise practice; final pitch to leadership Client access: Mediacharge enterprise clients, on request and case by case Research budget: €2,000, released for a defined purpose agreed with the supervisor Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow
